{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish concept in the first minute: a big side-view fish whose outline reads clearly and can be built as one run splitting round the body. I drew the pad sketches, including the redraw with the start moved to the nose, and I laid most of the top line along the back of the body. I also built the tail section and closed its crossing, so the tail end of the fish was in place before time ran out.

Execution: I worked steadily through the whole ten minutes. I laid the top line in short, continuous builds and inspected the nose area closely more than once to find where the fall was stalling. I rebuilt the links at the nose from the start and re-laid and finished the tail stroke in the last two minutes. In the final minute I stepped back from the table so nobody's hands were bumped.

Collaboration: I divided the work clearly: belly line, upper tail fork and lower tail fork each had an owner. I took Hana's suggestion to move the start to the nose and redrew the plan straight away. I kept the table informed and gave credit openly, to Sofia for the belly line and the nose checks, to Hana for the design catch and the top bridge, and to Omar for the upper fork. I also asked people to stay off areas I was rebuilding so we didn't undo each other's work.

Leadership: I set the direction early, assigned roles and kept the pace up with regular updates. I changed course quickly when a better plan came up, and I kept the group focused on dry runs and on the nose join as the deadline approached. I tried to keep the table energised and working together throughout. I think my share of the table's result was around 30%, with the rest coming from three teammates who each carried a major part of the build.", "my_share_percent": 30}
